notes: The URL is a copy of Ilford's sheet. Ilford's current edition (November 2018) prints the
same curve, for the same development, as a picture, which can't be read exactly; this
edition draws it as a vector path.
Characteristic curve: HP5 Plus 35 mm developed in ILFORD ILFOTEC HC (1+31) for 6 1/2
minutes at 20 °C with intermittent agitation, which the sheet says represents roll and
sheet film too. Its exposure axis is relative (log exposure from an arbitrary zero).
Log H ref, the grey card's exposure on that axis, is not printed. It is taken 1.01
(log10(8.125 / 0.8)) above the speed point, where the curve reaches 0.1 above base plus
fog (0.17, at its lowest exposure): 1.08, so 2.09. That is where ISO 6 puts a metered
midtone for a film whose speed is its foot speed; Ilford rates HP5 Plus at ISO 400 by
practical evaluation rather than foot speed, so this is approximate.
Page coordinates: the axes are calibrated from the plot's tick marks.
